chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ahmad ibn Suleyman, who said:

A man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was circumambulating (the Kaaba), and said to him: 'Inform me about 'al-Jawad' (the Benevolent/Generous).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your speech has two aspects. If you are asking about the created, then the 'Jawad' is the one who fulfills what Allah has obligated upon him. And if you are asking about the Creator, then He is the 'Jawad' if He gives, and He is the 'Jawad' if He withholds, because if He gives to you, He gives you what is not yours, and if He withholds from you, He withholds what is not for you.'

key_terms.الْجَوَادِ: The Benevolent or Generous (one who gives freely)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of 'al-Jawad' when applied to Allah versus created beings?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him) elucidates the semantic duality of 'al-Jawad' by distinguishing between the creature's duty to fulfill divine obligations and the Creator's absolute sovereignty in bestowing or withholding blessings. This theological nuance highlights that Allah’s generosity is not limited to giving, but extends to withholding as well, since both actions originate from His exclusive ownership and wisdom. This concept reinforces the Shia understanding of divine justice and grace, where human merit is secondary to God's ultimate discretion.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abu Al Jaham, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Ahmad Bin Suleyman who said,

‘A man asked Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st and heasws was in the circumambulation, so he said to himasws, ‘Inform me about ‘الْجَوَادِ’ the benevolence’. So heasws said: ‘For your speech there are two aspects. So, if you are asking about the people, so the benevolence is that which one fulfils what Allahazwj has Obligated upon him, and if you are asking about the Creator, so Heazwj is the ‘الْجَوَادِ’ Benevolent if Heazwj were to ‘السَّخَاءِ’ Give, and Heazwj is the Benevolent if Heasws was to prevent, because if Heazwj were to Give you, Heazwj Gives you what is not yours, and if Heazwj Prevents you, Heazwj Prevents you from what is not for you’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from, his father from abu al-Jahm from Musa ibn Bakr from Ahmad ibn Sulayman who has said the following: “

A man once asked abu al-Hassan, the 1st, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when he was performing Tawaf (walking seven times around the Ka‘bah), ‘Tell me about generosity.’ The Imam replied, ‘Your question has two sides. If you are asking about a generous creature, the answer is that a generous creature is one who pays what Allah has made obligatory on him to pay. If you are asking about the generosity of the Creator, then the answer is that the Creator is generous when He gives you something, and He is generous if He denies you something; if He gives you something, it does not belong to you; and if He denies you something, it does not belong to you.’”
